newsitem.title: JORDAN: Foreign buying in cement supports Jordan market.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying in cement supports Jordan market.

text.p: Jordan's bourse slipped slightly on Sunday but its fall was cushioned by a second day of strong foreign buying in the country's sole cement stock, dealers said.
Despite overall weak demand on most shares, market favourite Jordan Cement Factory rose 0.02 percent to 4.09 dinars in the busiest day's trade worth 521,624 dinars -- nearly half the day's trade.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.25 percent to 161.29 points in trade worth 1.1 million dinars ($1.5 million).

Dealers say the market is being underpinned by sporadic global international demand on Jordanian blue-chip even though the scope of emerging market fund buying has substantially fallen from high levels witnessed in May.
Foreign demand continues to bolster the market in the absence of strong local institutional demand, brokers said.
Arab Bank, which rose steeply over the last week in the wake of government plans to scrap a 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling, fell 1.00 dinars to 263 dinars in a price correction, dealers said.

"Foreign interest is still there, they are still accumulating shares and I expect a pickup once the 50 percent ceiling is abolished," said Samir Jaradat, investment manager of Jordan Investment and Finance Bank.

Investors expect Arab Bank, which already has reached its 50 percent ownership ceiling to become a target of fund buying once the planned amendments, which have still to be approved by cabinet, free up more shares for international buyers.
Overall 27 shares fell and only five rose on Sunday, while another 12 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance fell 0.23 percent to 80.97 points, 2.91 percent down from the start of the year.
